title: The Lord, Descending from Above
description: The Lord, Descending from Above in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 126, headed “God glorified in the gospel”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The Lord, de-scend-ing from a-bove, In-vites his child-ren near, While power and truth and bound-less love Dis-play their glo-ries here.

lines: While power and truth and boundless love
Here in thy gospel's wondrous frame
A thousand angels learn thy Name
Thy Name is writ in fairest lines,
Wisdom thro' all the mystery shines,
The law its best obedience owes
But still the lustre of thy grace
Gilds the whole scene with brighter rays,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
